newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE WINS MILLION DOLLAR TITLE IN PLAYOFF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE WINS MILLION DOLLAR TITLE IN PLAYOFF.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie scored the first playoff victory of his professional career when he beat Ernie Els on the third sudden-death hole to win the Million Dollar Challenge on Sunday.
The 33-year-old Scot, Europe's number one for four successive years, sank a five-foot birdie putt to win the giant jackpot at the third extra hole, the 18th at the Gary Player Country Club.
He and Els traded pars over the first two playoff holes before the 33-year-old Montgomerie sank a five-foot birdie putt at the 462-yard 18th.
His eight-iron approach into the green enjoyed a measure of good fortune when it bounced towards the pin off the bank on the right side 30 yards away.
"I had spoken with my caddy earlier and we agreed, if we were going to miss the green, we had to miss it right," Montgomerie said later. "I got fortunate but you've got to take it when it comes."
Els found thick rough on the left side of the green and was unable to hole his chip to keep the play-off alive.
Montgomerie said that victory, after poor showings here the last two years, was all the sweeter because of his previous poor record in play-offs.

"This was the sixth play-off of my career and I'd lost all five previous ones - two in majors and three in Europe. And it was great to beat Ernie in this one - although I still probably owe him one after the U.S. Open and the world matchplay!"

Els beat Montgomerie in a playoff to win the 1994 U.S. Open title and in the 1994 World Matchplay. Montgomerie also lost playoffs to Steve Elkington for the 1995 U.S. PGA, to Seve Ballesteros in the 1993 British PGA and to Irishman Philip Walton for the 1995 English Open.
Sunday's playoff, the third in the 16-year history of this event, was set up when Els, four shots off the pace overnight, charged up the field with a closing 66 - the low round of the day.
The South African did not drop a shot and he was then joined on 274, 14 under par, by Montgomerie, who also did not drop a shot in his 68.
U.S. Open champion Steve Jones shot a 70 to share third place with Zimbabwe's Nick Price, who closed with a 71 after sharing the lead with Ian Woosnam of Britain entering the final round.
Woosnam slipped to a 73 to tie for fifth with American Steve Stricker.

With three holes to play, Jones seemed headed for victory after a dramatic eagle three at the 14th where he holed out, via one bounce, from a greenside bunker. He then made a birdie three at the 15th to lead by a stroke.
But Jones dropped shots at 16 and 17 and missed a birdie putt at the last from seven feet which would have pushed him into a three-way playoff.
